slides.title:
AI tools
that save 10+ hours
a week
slides.subtitle: A practical carousel for developers who want faster shipping, cleaner code, and fewer context switches.

items.label: Focus
items.text: Use tools that remove repetitive work, not tools that add another workflow.

items.label: Promise
items.text: The best AI stack is invisible when you code and obvious when you measure velocity.

slides.footerLeft:
Swipe for the shortlist
built for real teams.
slides.cta:
Start with the tools
that actually compound.

slides.title:
1. Pair programming
with a copilot
slides.subtitle: Use autocomplete and chat in the same editor so you can move from idea to implementation without leaving context.

items.label: Best for
items.text: Feature work, refactors, and boilerplate that should never slow you down.

items.label: Try this
items.text: Ask for tests first, then request a safe implementation that matches the existing code style.

items.label: Watch out
items.text: If the output feels generic, tighten the prompt with repo-specific examples.

slides.footerLeft:
Reduce tab-switching.
Keep the editor as home base.

slides.title:
2. AI code review
before PRs land
slides.subtitle: Run a pre-merge pass that checks logic, style, edge cases, and missing tests before the team gets pulled into review.

items.label: Best for
items.text: Catching obvious defects early and turning code review into a higher-signal conversation.

items.label: Try this
items.text: Feed the diff plus the acceptance criteria, then ask for issues ranked by severity.

items.label: Watch out
items.text: Don’t let AI replace human judgment on product tradeoffs and architecture.

slides.footerLeft:
Shift review left.
Protect teammate attention.

slides.title:
3. Turn raw notes
into useful docs
slides.subtitle: Generate onboarding guides, API notes, and release summaries from commits, tickets, and meeting transcripts.

items.label: Best for
items.text: Teams that move quickly and need documentation to keep up.

items.label: Try this
items.text: Ask for a structure: what changed, why it changed, how to use it, and what to verify.

items.label: Watch out
items.text: Always link the source of truth so the docs stay auditable.

slides.cta:
Docs that stay
close to the code.

slides.title:
4. Add AI to
incident analysis
slides.subtitle: Use LLMs to summarize logs, cluster alerts, and draft postmortems while the team focuses on mitigation.

items.label: Best for
items.text: High-volume logs, noisy alerts, and recurring incident patterns.

items.label: Try this
items.text: Ask the model to extract timeline, blast radius, suspected root causes, and next actions.

items.label: Watch out
items.text: Keep observability data private and verify every claim against telemetry.

slides.footerLeft:
Turn chaos into
clear next steps.

slides.title:
Build a small AI stack
that compounds every sprint
slides.subtitle: Pick one editor helper, one review assistant, and one documentation workflow. Then measure saved time and quality gains.

items.label: Rule
items.text: Start small, keep the workflow close to the code, and remove anything that creates friction.

items.label: Goal
items.text: Make AI a reliable teammate for developers, not a separate destination.

slides.footerLeft:
